scope: Full AASM systematic review that supports the PAP guideline, replacing the abstract-only recommendation list.

keyRecommendations.text: PAP compared with no treatment reduces disease severity, sleepiness, blood pressure, and motor vehicle accidents, and improves sleep-related quality of life.
Starting PAP at home had equivalent effects to in-laboratory titration. Auto-adjusting or bilevel PAP did not differ in a clinically significant way from CPAP.
Educational, behavioral, troubleshooting, and telemonitoring interventions improved adherence. Nasal interfaces had better adherence than oronasal interfaces.

clinicalBottomLine: Use PAP rather than no treatment. Home initiation is equivalent to a laboratory titration in this review, CPAP and APAP are not clinically different, and education plus a nasal interface support adherence.
notableCaveats: Replaces the guideline abstract. This is the open full systematic review commissioned for that guideline.

source.title: Treatment of adult obstructive sleep apnea with positive airway pressure: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine systematic review, meta-analysis, and GRADE assessment.
